about: Frozen gold labels for the portable ard-kit retrieval benchmark.
Each query lists the tools that are a CORRECT answer; several may be
correct (multi-gold), so a tie between two fitting tools is a pass, not
an arbitrary pick. Gold keys are the identifier tail after
'urn:air:<domain>:' so they stay valid whatever domain the corpus is
Labels were authored against the REAL production scorer output
(ard_kit.registry.search_catalog) over the fixture corpus, not predicted.
The ru group documents a measured cross-lingual limitation of the
stem-folded token-overlap scorer; it is reported honestly, NOT fixed here.

groups.name: ru
groups.about: Russian queries, reported as their own group. kind=cyrillic-blind queries are pure Cyrillic, which the [a-z0-9]+ tokenizer reduces to an empty token set: the scorer then returns the WHOLE catalog at score 0 and the intended tool is NOT ranked (matched=0). kind=latin-rescue queries carry a latin/acronym token (csv, json, pdf) that survives tokenization and rescues the correct tool. This contrast is the honest headline finding, measured not fixed.

queries.q: подсчитать слова и строки в файле
queries.note: Pure Cyrillic -> empty token set -> all 13 rows at score 0; intended tool not ranked.
Pure Cyrillic -> tokenizer-blind; whole catalog returned at score 0.
Latin tokens {csv,json} survive; csv_to_json ranks first.
Only latin token is {json}; json_validate and csv_to_json TIE at max score, identifier tie-break puts json_validate first. Single-token reduction is a scorer artifact, reported honestly.
Latin token {pdf} survives; pdf-extract is the unique match.

groups.name: negative
groups.about: Absent-capability queries: the corpus has no tool for these. A correct scorer returns an empty result (totalResults=0), i.e. it can say 'no such capability'. Every content token is outside the corpus vocabulary and none is a stopword, so the query tokenizes non-empty and the score<=0 filter fires.
